declared.title: Effectiveness of different types of mental simulation in the weight loss process based on a perseverance study among people with different BMI
declared.foundIn: reports/choose-your-struggle/counter-evidence.md (card 5); OpenAlex search « Styk Zmorzyński Klinkosz process simulation outcome simulation » (2026-11-26)

population: 252 adults recruited online by a Polish team, of different BMI, given a process or an outcome simulation before a maze test

findings.text: After rehearsing the process rather than the outcome, people solved more maze tasks and spent more time on the test

support.sentence: Process simulation subjects completed more tasks and spent more time solving the test than outcome simulation subjects.

limits: perseverance on easy online mazes right after a short instruction, with unlimited attempts and a quit button: not a real-life goal
assignment described both as random and as alternating (full text): quasi-random, not masked; small effect (η² = .03)
very skewed outcomes reported as normal (SD 89 for a mean of 90 tasks, 611 for 687 s); F(1) = 8.32 reported with p < .001 (about .004 with ≈ 246 df)
no group without simulation; weight and height self-reported; despite the title, no weight measured
no sample from the Middle East or North Africa
